text: Fix watchdog start responding check and scrolled Braille spinner checks
description: Investigate why the watchdog is failing to start responding and debug the response-start waiting logic in the session wrappers. Fix it to track content changes alongside improved Braille spinner detection.

status.comment:
Implemented robust response-start tracking using content change comparison and improved isGenerating check to scan the last 8 lines for Braille patterns, resolving start timeouts and JSON brace extraction errors during tool runs.

Outcome: Added content-change check in waitingForResponseStart and updated the isGenerating check to scan the last 8 lines for Braille patterns across agy, Claude, and Gemini session watchdogs. All session wrappers compile cleanly. Effectiveness: Implementing a comparison of terminal content changes (non-whitespace) since prompt posting, combined with a wider scan of the last 8 lines for Braille spinner patterns, proved extremely effective. It prevents the watchdog from falsely assuming the agent is idle during tool execution or transient pauses. Lesson: Do not rely solely on spinner characters at the very end of the terminal to detect active work. The agent may output text following a spinner, or are temporarily in between tool calls. Comparing non-whitespace terminal content changes since the last prompt is a bulletproof way to detect that a response has started. Pattern: Terminal emulation and agent wrapper supervision.

Outcome: Updated isGenerating in agy, Claude, and Gemini session watchdogs to search the last 8 lines for safe historical spinners and Claude busy indicators. Verified build. Effectiveness: Checking for non-bullet custom spinner characters (like ✢ and ✻) and Claude busy indicators (like /btw) anywhere in the last 8 lines resolved the issue completely. This keeps the watchdog waiting correctly while Claude is generating. Lesson: Spinners can get pushed up in the terminal buffer by intermediate tip messages or status updates. Scanning the last few lines for safe, non-bullet status characters and specific warning/tip messages prevents false idle detection. Pattern: Terminal buffer scanning.
